_**User**_

I need a better way to handle upcoming pages and drafts

---

_**Assistant**_



There are several good patterns for handling drafts and upcoming content in Astro. Here's a recommended approach:

1. **Use frontmatter to manage post status**. Instead of separate directories, you can keep all posts in one place and use metadata to control their visibility:

```mdx:src/content/posts/example-post.mdx
---
title: "My Post"
status: "draft" // or "published" or "scheduled"
publishDate: "2024-04-01"
---
```

2. **Create a collection schema** to enforce these fields:

```typescript:src/content/config.ts
import { defineCollection, z } from 'astro:content';

const posts = defineCollection({
  schema: z.object({
    title: z.string(),
    status: z.enum(['draft', 'published', 'scheduled']),
    publishDate: z.date(),
    // ... other fields
  })
});

export const collections = { posts };
```

3. **Filter posts based on environment and status**:

```typescript:src/utils/posts.ts
const isProd = import.meta.env.PROD;

export async function getVisiblePosts() {
  const posts = await getCollection('posts');
  
  return posts.filter(post => {
    // In development, show everything
    if (!isProd) return true;
    
    // In production:
    if (post.data.status === 'draft') return false;
    if (post.data.status === 'scheduled' && 
        new Date(post.data.publishDate) > new Date()) return false;
    
    return true;
  }).sort((a, b) => 
    new Date(b.data.publishDate).getTime() - 
    new Date(a.data.publishDate).getTime()
  );
}
```

This approach gives you several benefits:
- All content stays in one place
- Drafts won't show in production
- Scheduled posts automatically appear on their publish date
- You can easily preview drafts in development
- Better TypeScript support with the schema
